segments.text: This is Rune. A word processor for Linux that writes with you.

segments.caption: Native editing
segments.text: It opens real documents: OpenDocument, Word, even old dot-doc files. And it feels quick, because it's native. One process, no browser inside.

segments.caption: The outline
segments.text: Writing a book? Chapters are just headings. The outline shows every chapter and scene, with its word count. Drag one, and the whole chapter moves with it.

segments.caption: Story notes
segments.text: Characters, places and research live in the same file as story notes, so they travel with your manuscript.

segments.caption: AI edits in place
segments.text: Select a passage and say what you want. The AI edits the page in place, keeps your formatting, and the whole change is a single undo.

segments.caption: AI writes at the cursor
segments.text: Or ask it to pick up where you left off. It reads your story notes, so it knows who your characters are.

segments.caption: Your own AI accounts
segments.text: Sign in with the ChatGPT plan you already pay for, or reach Claude, GPT and Grok through OpenRouter. Rune has no server of its own, and your sign-in stays in your keyring.

segments.caption: Citations
segments.text: Writing a paper? Add your sources, or paste BibTeX, then cite as you write, in APA, MLA, Chicago or IEEE. Switch styles, and every citation follows. The bibliography keeps itself up to date.

segments.caption: Command palette
segments.text: Everything else is a keystroke away. Press Control K, and just type.
Rune is free and open source, made for Omarchy. Get it at rune dot ninepointlabs dot com.
